title: `is` tests a value against a type, answers `bool`, and is total
scope:
the `is` operator, the type forms it accepts, the three it refuses, and the narrowing it
performs. It decides nothing about *patterns* — destructuring, array shapes, comparison patterns,
pinning, binding — which § 7 reserves and does not design.

summary.headline: `$x is T` asks whether a value holds a type, and always answers `bool`
summary.body:
`$x is User` is true when the value currently holds a `User`, and inside the branch it guards
the value is treated as one. It always compiles, even where the answer is knowable in advance,
and it never throws. It closes the gap beside `as ?T`, which asks whether a value can become a
type rather than whether it is one. The spelling follows PHP's own pattern-matching proposal for
the type-test case; the pattern forms PHP has not settled on are left unclaimed, so a future PHP
program will not mean something different here.
